title: Section 326 — Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc

content.overview: Section 326 — Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc. The operative rule is the text of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 435 / 436. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024. enhancement.definition:
BNS s. 326 governs Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc. It provides: Whoever commits mischief by,
(a) doing any act which causes, or which he knows to be likely to cause, a diminution of the supply of water for agricultural purposes, or for food or drink for human beings or for animals which are property, or for cleanliness or for carrying on any manufacture, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Safeguards the legal order under Chapter XVII (Of Offences against Property) by establishing clear statutory boundaries, penal deterrence, and accountability for mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc.

Core Legal Mandate: Whoever commits mischief by,
(a) doing any act which causes, or which he knows to be likely to cause, a diminution of the supply of water for agricultural purposes, or for food or drink for human bein...
Classification and Sentencing: Structured under Chapter XVII penal tiers.
Evidentiary and Procedural Cognate: Governed by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
essentialIngredients: (a) doing any act which causes, or which he knows to be likely to cause, a diminution of the supply of water for agricultural purposes, or for food or drink for human beings or for animals which are property, or for cleanliness or for carrying on any manufacture, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both

(b) doing any act which renders or which he knows to be likely to render any public road, bridge, navigable river or navigable channel, natural or artificial, impassable or less safe for travelling or conveying property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both

(c) doing any act which causes or which he knows to be likely to cause an inundation or an obstruction to any public drainage attended with injury or damage, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 326 constitutes a key component of Chapter XVII (Of Offences against Property) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc under Section 326 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 326.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 326 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 326 vs General Attempt: Section 326 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XVII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.
Section 326 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 326 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences against Property.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 326 for conduct relating to mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc.
Rule: Under BNS s. 326, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 326.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 326 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
